content.title: How is Cricket Played?
content.text: Cricket is not just a sport; it is one of the trendiest passions among masses all over the world. From local towns to huge arenas, cricket brings into view an exciting and skillful activity that includes strategy and teamwork. If ever you have speculated how one plays cricket, let's break the concept down. how is cricket played What is Cricket?Cricket is a team game involving two teams, each having eleven players. It is a game between two teams for a higher score. Cricket actually originated in England during the 16th century and finally took the position of an international game. Nowadays, cricket is one of the most-watched games in the world. Some of the events like ICC Cricket World Cup and Indian Premier League assembled people from over borders. Cricket Field SetupA good understanding of the playing field more than anything gives a great deal in understanding how cricket is played. Generally an oval field, it contains a rectangular pitch at the centre where most of the action is concentrated. While the length of the pitch is 22 yards, its width is quite significant to both bowling and batting. Dimensions of the FieldField of play The field of play shall be an area 70 yards by distance between boundaries.The pitch: The playing area proper, within the stumps-three upright wooden posts, extends from one end of the pitch to 22 yards in the other. Important parts of the field Wickets: Three stumps standing at each end of the pitch form a target for bowlers and a focal point generally for the fielders.Boundary: The field's outermost line. Hitting the ball over this line scores four or six runs, depending on whether the ball touches the ground.Players and RolesEach player of a cricket team has a particular role when he is batting, bowling, or fielding. BatsmenThe batsmen essentially are the ones who try to score runs by hitting the ball. At any time, there are usually two batsmen out in the middle, one at each end of the pitch. BowlersThe bowlers try to get the batsmen out by bowling the ball in a way such that it either hits the stumps or the batsman edges the ball into the hands of the fielders. FieldersThe fielders also stop the ball and catch, or throw it back either to the wicketkeeper or to the stumps. WicketkeeperThe wicketkeeper stands behind the stumps. He catches balls which the batsman misses or by which he is dismissed. Types of Cricket MatchesThere are several types of cricket matches with varied rules and pace of the game: Test MatchIt's the longest format, lasting for five days, in which each team gets to bat twice. It's definitely the format that allows the full strategic depth of the game to be expressed. One Day InternationalsIn ODIs it goes for just one day, having 50 overs per side. The pace of the game is faster; hence it's more amenable to casual viewers. Twenty20T20 format is the shortest per side, consisting of 20 overs being used up. Action is brisk and it generally lasts not more than three hours in total.EquipmentLet me now talk about the equipment that is essentially required to play this game.Bat and BallThe bat is of wood and is used by the batsman to hit the ball. The cricket ball is hard and leather-covered most of the time but has a core of cork.Safety EquipmentPlayers wear safety equipment: helmets, gloves, pads and a box if male to prevent injury.How Cricket is Played: The RulesIntroduction to the format of the matchCricket is a game in an innings format. Both the teams get the opportunity to bat and bowl. While the batting team tries to score runs, the bowling along with fielding team tries to stop runs and gets the batsmen out.The TossBefore the match gets underway, captains go for a coin toss on deciding whether they can bat or bowl first. The outcome of the toss sets up a way as to how teams strategize whether the weather or pitch conditions are favorable. The Batting Side: How Batting WorksBatting TechniquesHe plays different shots-drive, pull and cut-all for runs. But his central aim is to save the wicket but simultaneously trying to make boundaries off the ball. Runs ScoringSingles: These are runs between the wickets after the ball has been hit.Fours: This is a hit along the ground that goes over a boundary.Over-the-boundary hits without the ball ever touching the ground are called Sixes.Type of RunsRuns in cricket can be made between the wickets, at boundaries and on extras which are based on no-balls as well as wides.The Bowling Team : Game of BowlingTypes of BowlingBowling itself is an art that requires much ability in skill and execution. The bowlers plot to get him out by either bowling a perfectly straightforward or using variations from spin or swingsValue of StrategyIn order to outwit the batsmen, bowling strategies become imperative. The fast bowlers bank upon speed whereas the spinners bank upon deception and movement. Types of Bowling: Fast, Spin etc.Fast Bowling: It banks on the pace and bounce.Spin Bowling: depends upon making the ball turn off the pitch to outwit the batsman.Fielding Side: The Art of FieldingFielding is the most important salient feature of the game. A well-timed catch or run-out often changes the tide of the game. Fielding PositionsThe fielders stand in different positions either to stop the ball or catch it. The wicketkeeper stands behind the stumps while the other fielders stand at positions known as slips, covers, and mid-on. Skilled FieldingA good fielder has got to be highly coordinated with his hand and eye, agile and throw the ball at the target. Role of the UmpiresTheir role in a game is to make sure the game is fair and all the rules of the game observed. Decision MakingThey decide whether the batsman is out or a ball is a no-ball or wide. The Third UmpireEven the third umpire these days could resort to the technology so as to review decisions by the on-field umpires.Scoring in Cricket How to Understand Runs and ExtrasExtras Extras are those runs that are awarded to the batting team when some kind of error has been committed on the part of the bowler, such as a no-ball or wide. How Runs Are ScoredEvery time the batsman successfully runs across the wickets or, for that matter, hits the ball for a boundary, he scores runs for his team.How a Cricket Match is WonThe winner in a cricket match is the team that scores the highest runs, though the winning conditions may vary with respect to the format. Strategies and Tactics in CricketCricket is not about just hitting the ball and then running for runs. A couple of strategies are involved in this game by a team, which ranges from field placements to aggressive attacks either with the bat or ball. Offensive and Defensive StrategiesThe success key in cricket lies in the fine balance between attack and defense. Importance of TeamworkThe successful teams in cricket are integrated units, where every player has to do a particular job in the overall strategy. ConclusionCricket is that kind of game that can change from grueling to really exciting within that very moment, where every single nuance of it means something: full of action, with nuances galore, an importantly strategic game. From the high-octane action in contests of T20 cricket down to the relative languidness of Test cricket, the essential ingredients remain absolutely unchanged: a heavy dose of skill, strategy, and teamwork. Accordingly, with growing globalization, this sport happens to evolve in new ways and does retain its charms from yore. Cricket is a team game; two teams happen to be involved in this game, one team contains 11 players, whereas the other contains another 11. In cricket basically, the main motive is to have a bigger score as compared to the other team. Cricket is divided into batting, bowling, and fielding.How long does an average match of cricket take? Well, that depends upon the format of the game: Test matches may last up to five days, ODIs approximately 8 hours while T20s will get finished in about 3 hours.What is the wicketkeeper in cricket? He is behind the stumps and is supposed to catch balls which the batsman misses and effect stumpings or run-outs.How are runs scored in cricket? Runs come to the team by hitting the ball and running between the wickets or hit boundaries-four or six. What is "no-ball" in cricket? No-ball is a kind of illegitimate delivery mainly because of overstepping the crease or bowling dangerously.
